title: Plant Manager / Plant Incharge
summary: Lead end-to-end plant operations to deliver the right concrete, at the right time and cost, while protecting people, assets, quality and the environment. Own plant-level production, service, cost, team performance and profitability outcomes.
responsibilities:
Production planning and dispatch
Translate confirmed orders and pour schedules into daily/shift production plans; align batching capacity, raw-material availability, transit mixers and pumps; monitor order changes and prevent avoidable waiting or missed deliveries.
KPIs: Production plan adherence; plant utilisation; on-time-in-full delivery; m³ produced per shift.

Cost and plant profitability
Track cost per m³, material consumption, wastage, diesel, power, maintenance, overtime and fleet / pump costs; investigate variances and implement corrective actions without compromising specification or safety.
KPIs: Cost per m³ vs budget; contribution / plant profitability; material variance; concrete wastage.

Quality and customer service
Ensure production only against approved mix designs and order specifications; coordinate with Technical / QA-QC for material acceptance, moisture correction, slump and strength issues; close complaints with documented root-cause and corrective action.
KPIs: Rejection / complaint rate; complaint closure time; quality-related wastage; customer service score.

Asset reliability and maintenance
Ensure preventive maintenance and breakdown escalation for batching plant, mixer, silos, conveyors, compressors, DG, loader, weighbridge, transit mixers and pumps; verify calibration and maintenance records.
KPIs: Plant downtime; preventive-maintenance compliance; equipment availability; calibration compliance.

Materials and inventory
Review stock cover and consumption forecasts for cementitious materials, aggregates, sand, admixtures, diesel and critical spares; prevent stockouts, excess inventory, pilferage and unrecorded consumption.
KPIs: Stockout incidents; inventory accuracy; stock variance; emergency purchases.

People and productivity
Set shift rosters and responsibilities; monitor attendance, competency, training, discipline and productivity; develop multi-skilling and succession cover for critical roles.
KPIs: Manpower productivity; training completion; absenteeism; competency / Kaushal scores where used.

Safety, environment and compliance
Enforce PPE, traffic management, machine guarding, permit-to-work and safe loading / unloading; report incidents and near misses; control dust, wash water, slurry and waste; maintain applicable statutory and environmental records.
KPIs: Safety observations and incident closure; audit findings; environmental non-conformities; compliance completion.

Systems and reporting
Maintain accurate ERP / batch records, production and dispatch logs, downtime reports, consumption reconciliations, customer complaints and daily / monthly MIS; act on trends rather than only reporting them.
KPIs: MIS accuracy and timeliness; ERP transaction compliance; audit observations; action closure.
qualification: B.E./B.Tech or Diploma in Civil, Mechanical or Electrical Engineering; equivalent RMC experience may be considered
other_requirements:
Function: Plant Operations
Reports to: Business Manager / Business Head / Area Operations Head
Working relationships: Batching Plant Operators, Material / Operations Officer, Plant Technical Officer (functional coordination), dispatch / customer coordination staff, plant technicians and other assigned plant personnel.
Experience: Typically 5–8+ years in RMC / concrete operations, including plant-level responsibility; exact threshold to be aligned to plant scale.
Key interfaces: Business / Sales, Technical / QA-QC, Logistics / Dispatch, Procurement, Accounts, HR / IR, customers, raw-material suppliers, fleet and maintenance vendors.
Work environment: Plant-based role; shift / extended-hour availability may be required during major pours, breakdowns or service recovery. Travel between plants may be required.
Role-specific governance: The role is accountable for documented reviews, assigned corrective actions and escalation of material risks. Delegated financial, people, safety and operational authorities must be followed.

title: Sales Officer / Sales Executive (RMC)
summary: Generate profitable RMC business by developing customer relationships, converting qualified opportunities, securing repeat orders and ensuring disciplined commercial follow-up and collections.
responsibilities:
Market mapping and lead generation
Map builders, developers, infrastructure contractors, consultants, architects and individual-house-builder opportunities in the assigned territory; identify upcoming projects, competitors, concrete demand and decision-makers.
KPIs: Qualified leads; pipeline value; new accounts opened; site / customer meetings.

Opportunity conversion
Qualify demand, grade / volume / pour schedule, site access, payment terms, competitor position and credit risk; coordinate technical presentations, trials and quotations; follow the approval process for pricing and commercial terms.
KPIs: Lead-to-order conversion; order book; win rate; sales cycle.

Revenue and margin delivery
Achieve assigned monthly / quarterly volume, revenue and contribution targets; avoid unapproved discounts and low-margin commitments; provide realistic demand forecasts to operations.
KPIs: Sales volume; revenue; contribution / gross margin; forecast accuracy.

Customer relationship and service recovery
Maintain regular contact with site engineers, purchase teams, contractors and consultants; coordinate complaints, supply interruptions and technical issues with relevant teams; communicate commitments accurately.
KPIs: Repeat business; customer retention; complaint closure; customer feedback.

Order coordination
Confirm order details, grade, quantity, delivery windows, site access, pump requirements and payment status before commitment; coordinate with plant and dispatch to avoid overbooking or infeasible promises.
KPIs: Order accuracy; cancellation rate; service-level performance.

Receivables and credit discipline
Follow up on due invoices and disputes; obtain payment commitments; escalate overdue accounts and credit-limit breaches; coordinate ledger reconciliation with Accounts; do not promise credit exceptions without approval.
KPIs: Collections vs target; overdue receivables; DSO; disputed invoices resolved.

Market intelligence and reporting
Maintain CRM / sales tracker, site visit reports, opportunity stage, competitor pricing, project updates, lost-order reasons and collection plans; submit accurate forecasts and weekly review inputs.
KPIs: CRM hygiene; report timeliness; pipeline coverage; forecast accuracy.
qualification: Graduate in any discipline; civil engineering / construction or business qualification is an advantage
other_requirements:
Function: Sales & Business Development
Reports to: Sales Manager / Business Manager
Working relationships: Normally none; coordinates closely with plant, technical, logistics and accounts teams.
Experience: Typically 2–5 years of field sales experience; building materials, cement, aggregates or RMC experience preferred. Two-wheeler and valid driving licence where field travel requires it.
Key interfaces: Business Head, plant operations, Technical / QA-QC, Logistics / Dispatch, Accounts / Credit Control, procurement where required, customers, contractors and consultants.
Work environment: Field-based role with frequent site visits and local travel. Targets, territory, incentive plan, employment type and travel reimbursement should be stated in the vacancy-specific posting.
Role-specific governance: Pricing exceptions, credit terms, customer commitments and claims must remain within delegated authority. Sales forecasts and collection status must be supported by current customer / project information.

title: Plant Technical Incharge / Technical Incharge
summary: Own technical governance for concrete quality across assigned plant(s), ensuring approved mix designs, raw-material control, testing discipline, strength and workability performance, customer technical support and continuous mix-cost optimisation.
responsibilities:
Mix design and technical control
Develop, validate, review and control mix designs for specified grades and performance requirements; ensure production uses the current approved mix design and authorised revisions only; coordinate trials and customer approvals.
KPIs: Approved mix-design compliance; trial success rate; mix-design turnaround time.

Raw-material quality
Establish testing and acceptance controls for cementitious materials, aggregates / sand, water and admixtures; review certificates and test trends; investigate supplier / source changes and non-conforming material; coordinate corrective action with procurement and plant teams.
KPIs: Incoming material test compliance; non-conformance closure; source qualification status.

Fresh and hardened concrete quality
Set testing plans for workability / slump, temperature where specified, sampling, specimen preparation, curing and compressive-strength testing; review 7-day / 28-day results and trends; initiate investigation when results deviate from requirements.
KPIs: Strength compliance; slump / workability non-conformance; testing completion and record accuracy.

Technical customer support
Attend technical meetings and site visits; clarify specifications and placement constraints; support trials, pour monitoring and investigation of complaints; issue clear technical findings without assigning unsupported blame.
KPIs: Technical complaint closure time; repeat quality complaints; customer technical feedback.

Mix optimisation and cost
Run controlled trials to optimise cementitious content, aggregate grading, admixture dosage and alternative approved materials while meeting performance requirements; quantify savings and obtain approvals before implementation.
KPIs: Verified mix-cost savings per m³; raw-material-to-sales ratio; performance stability.

Process control and calibration
Audit batching accuracy, moisture corrections, weighing and dosing systems, plant calibration, sampling equipment and laboratory practices; work with Plant Manager to correct process drift.
KPIs: Calibration compliance; batching / moisture correction compliance; audit findings.

Documentation and standards
Maintain mix designs, test registers, calibration records, material approvals, non-conformance reports, customer reports and technical SOPs; apply relevant current Indian Standards and project specifications.
KPIs: Document completeness; audit closure; report turnaround.

Capability building
Train operators, plant staff, sales and customer-facing teams on concrete basics, sampling, slump control, mix handling and quality escalation; support technical induction.
KPIs: Training completion; assessment results; reduction in repeat errors.
required_skills: relevant IS standards and project specifications
qualification: B.E./B.Tech or Diploma in Civil Engineering; concrete technology / materials testing experience is essential
other_requirements:
Function: Technical / Quality
Reports to: Head – Technical / Quality; functional coordination with Business Head and Plant Manager
Working relationships: Plant Technical Officers, laboratory technicians and other quality resources as assigned.
Experience: Typically 4–8 years for an in-charge role, with substantial RMC laboratory / technical experience.
Key interfaces: Plant Manager, Plant Technical Officers, Sales, Logistics / Dispatch, Procurement, suppliers, customer QA/QC teams, consultants and external laboratories.
Work environment: Plant and customer-site visits; may need to attend critical pours, investigations or testing outside normal office hours.
Role-specific governance: The role must use approved technical procedures, applicable current Indian Standards and project specifications. Material rejection, mix-design revision and technical concessions must follow documented authority and escalation routes.

title: Batching Plant Operator / Batcher
summary: Operate the batching system safely and accurately to produce concrete strictly to the approved mix design and order instructions, while maintaining batch records, plant housekeeping and reliable dispatch coordination.
responsibilities:
Batching and production
Verify order, grade, quantity and approved mix; select the correct mix code; operate batching controls and ensure cement, aggregates, water and admixtures are batched within approved tolerances; never override a recipe without authorisation.
KPIs: Batching accuracy; batch cycle time; production output; batch rejection / exception rate.

Moisture and workability control
Use authorised aggregate-moisture inputs and approved corrections; coordinate with Technical / QA-QC on slump or workability deviations; do not add water or admixture outside approved instructions.
KPIs: Moisture-entry accuracy; slump-related rejection; unauthorised adjustments (target zero).

Batch records and ERP
Record production, batch tickets, material consumption, exceptions, downtime and dispatch information accurately in the plant system / ERP; promptly report discrepancies.
KPIs: Batch record accuracy; ERP compliance; exception closure.

Equipment checks and housekeeping
Complete pre-start checks; monitor load cells, sensors, conveyors, mixer, gates, water and admixture dosing; clean mixer and cabin as per SOP; carry out only authorised routine checks and isolate unsafe equipment.
KPIs: Pre-start checklist completion; avoidable downtime; housekeeping score.

Dispatch coordination
Coordinate with dispatch for truck sequence, load size, loading status and final load; communicate delays, equipment faults and batch exceptions promptly.
KPIs: Loading turnaround time; dispatch plan adherence; communication errors.

Safety and environmental care
Follow machine guarding, lockout / isolation, PPE, traffic and dust-control rules; prevent overflow and spills; manage washout only at designated locations; report unsafe conditions and near misses.
KPIs: Safety compliance; spill / housekeeping incidents; incident reporting timeliness.

Energy and resource use
Switch off idle equipment and DG as authorised; avoid unnecessary re-batching, material spillage and concrete waste; report abnormal power / fuel use.
KPIs: Energy use per m³; concrete wastage; avoidable re-batching.
qualification: ITI / Diploma in Mechanical, Electrical, Instrumentation or related discipline; science / technical graduates may also be considered
other_requirements:
Function: Plant Operations
Reports to: Plant Manager / Plant Incharge; shift-wise coordination with Dispatch and Technical / QA-QC
Working relationships: None.
Experience: Typically 1–3 years of relevant plant / batching experience, with training and authorisation required before independent operation.
Key interfaces: Plant Manager, dispatchers, Plant Technical / QA-QC, Material / Operations Officer, transit-mixer drivers and maintenance technicians.
Work environment: Shift-based plant role; may require rotational shifts, weekends and extended hours based on pour schedules.
Role-specific governance: No unauthorised recipe, weighing, water or admixture adjustment is permitted. Equipment faults, abnormal batches and safety risks must be escalated and recorded before production resumes.

title: Material / Operations Officer
summary: Ensure uninterrupted plant operations through disciplined receipt, verification, inventory control and issue of raw materials, fuel and spares, accurate ERP records, weighbridge control and coordination of assigned plant resources.
responsibilities:
Material receipt and documentation
Verify purchase order / delivery details, vehicle and weighment records, quantity and visible condition of incoming materials; coordinate sampling and acceptance with Technical / QA-QC; record receipts in ERP promptly and accurately.
KPIs: Receipt-entry timeliness; weighment accuracy; documentation completeness; quantity variance.

Inventory and stock planning
Maintain daily stock records for cementitious materials, aggregates, sand, admixtures and diesel; conduct physical stock measurements at defined frequency; compare physical stock with book stock and investigate variances.
KPIs: Inventory accuracy; stock variance; stockout incidents; stock-cover adherence.

Procurement follow-up and stockouts
Forecast consumption using production plans and stock cover; follow up approved purchase orders and delivery schedules; escalate low stock and supplier delays early; avoid unauthorised purchases.
KPIs: Emergency procurement; stockout downtime; forecast accuracy.

Spares, oils and consumables
Maintain controlled records for critical spares and consumables; issue against authorised requests and record at time of issue; reconcile physical stock with ERP; follow approved storage and oil-management practices.
KPIs: Spares reconciliation; unrecorded issues (target zero); obsolete / excess inventory.

Weighbridge control
Ensure weighbridge is used correctly, records are traceable and calibration / maintenance is current; flag suspected tampering, abnormal weights or mismatches for investigation.
KPIs: Weighbridge availability; calibration compliance; weighment discrepancy rate.

Plant resource coordination
Support planning and availability of transit mixers, loader, DG and other assigned resources; coordinate maintenance requests and utilisation records with the Plant Manager.
KPIs: Resource availability; utilisation; idle time; breakdown escalation time.

Housekeeping and safety
Maintain organised storage areas, safe stacking, access routes, spill control and material identification; follow safe handling procedures for cement, admixtures, diesel and oils.
KPIs: Housekeeping audit score; safety observations; spill / storage non-conformities.

MIS and reconciliation
Prepare daily material consumption and stock reports; reconcile receipts, issues, production consumption and physical stock; maintain audit-ready records and support internal / statutory audits.
KPIs: Report timeliness; reconciliation closure; audit observations.
qualification: Diploma / B.E. in Mechanical, Electrical, Instrumentation or Civil Engineering; graduates with relevant materials / plant operations experience may be considered
other_requirements:
Function: Plant Operations / Materials
Reports to: Plant Manager / Plant Incharge
Working relationships: Store / weighbridge / support staff where assigned; coordinates with loader, transit-mixer and DG teams as applicable.
Experience: Typically 2–4 years of relevant experience; ERP and weighbridge exposure preferred.
Key interfaces: Plant Manager, Technical / QA-QC, Procurement, Accounts, batching operators, suppliers, transporters and maintenance vendors.
Work environment: Plant-based role with routine outdoor work and physical stock verification.
Role-specific governance: All receipts, weighments and issues must be recorded at the time of transaction. Any stock / weighment discrepancy, suspected tampering or quality concern must be reported promptly.

title: Business Manager / Business Head
summary: Own business growth and operating performance for an assigned territory, cluster or business unit by delivering profitable sales, customer retention, plant performance, cash collection, safety, quality and talent outcomes.
responsibilities:
Business plan and profitable growth
Translate annual targets into territory, customer, plant and product plans; review demand, capacity and competitive conditions; prioritise sustainable volume and contribution rather than volume alone.
KPIs: Revenue and volume vs plan; contribution / EBITDA; market share where measurable.

Sales pipeline and key accounts
Build relationships with strategic customers, developers, contractors and consultants; review pipeline quality, major bids, pricing, win/loss reasons and concentration risk; approve commercial commitments within delegated authority.
KPIs: Pipeline coverage; new-account acquisition; key-account retention; win rate.

Pricing, margin and credit
Set / review pricing and discount discipline within approved authority; evaluate freight, pumping, material and service costs; review credit exposure and overdue receivables with Accounts; escalate exceptions.
KPIs: Contribution per m³; price realisation; DSO; overdue debt; bad-debt exposure.

Plant and service performance
Review production capacity, cost per m³, plant utilisation, downtime, quality complaints, delivery reliability and customer service across plants; remove cross-functional bottlenecks and assign action owners.
KPIs: Plant profitability; cost variance; on-time delivery; quality complaints; utilisation.

People and organisation
Set objectives for managers; build succession and technical / commercial capability; review manpower, productivity, attendance, performance and retention; maintain a culture of accountability and safe behaviour.
KPIs: Goal achievement; critical-role coverage; training / succession actions; regretted attrition.

Safety, quality and governance
Ensure operating leaders implement safety, environmental, quality and compliance controls; review significant incidents, customer claims, audit findings and corrective actions; do not trade off compliance for output.
KPIs: Incident closure; audit action closure; compliance status; repeat non-conformities.

Business reviews and forecasting
Lead monthly business reviews using sales, margin, receivables, production, fleet, quality and cost data; ensure forecast assumptions are evidence-based and actions have owners and due dates.
KPIs: Forecast accuracy; review action closure; MIS quality and timeliness.

Expansion and continuous improvement
Assess new plant / territory opportunities, capacity constraints, customer economics and investment proposals; sponsor productivity, digitisation, sustainability and waste-reduction initiatives.
KPIs: New business contribution; payback of approved initiatives; verified savings.
qualification: Graduate / engineering degree; MBA or commercial / operations qualification is an advantage
other_requirements:
Function: Business / Regional Operations
Reports to: Regional Head / Business Director / senior management
Working relationships: Plant Managers, Sales Managers / Officers and assigned functional or cluster teams.
Experience: Typically 8–12+ years in RMC, cement, building materials or allied construction markets, with demonstrated multi-function or business responsibility.
Key interfaces: Senior management, Sales, Plant Operations, Technical / QA-QC, Logistics, Procurement, Finance / Accounts, HR / IR, customers, suppliers and local authorities as relevant.
Work environment: Multi-plant / territory travel; availability for major customer escalations and operational incidents.
Role-specific governance: The role is accountable for documented reviews, assigned corrective actions and escalation of material risks. Delegated financial, people, safety and operational authorities must be followed.

title: Accounts Incharge / Plant Accounts Incharge
summary: Maintain accurate plant / area financial records and controls, ensure timely vendor and customer accounting, support statutory reporting and audits, and provide reliable MIS for cost, working capital and business decisions.
responsibilities:
Accounts payable and vendor controls
Verify invoices against purchase orders, receipts / service confirmations and approvals; ensure correct accounting, tax treatment and timely booking; manage vendor advances, reconciliations and payment proposals.
KPIs: Invoice turnaround; duplicate / exception rate; vendor reconciliation ageing; payment timeliness.

Sales accounting and receivables
Ensure timely and accurate sales invoicing; reconcile customer ledgers; track receipts, credit notes, deductions and disputed invoices; coordinate collection follow-up and escalation with Sales.
KPIs: Invoice accuracy; billing timeliness; unapplied receipts; overdue receivables / DSO.

Plant cost and inventory accounting
Review material, diesel, power, repairs, fleet / pump, labour and other plant costs; reconcile consumption / stock records with operations; investigate abnormal variances and support cost-per-m³ reporting.
KPIs: Cost-report timeliness; reconciliation closure; cost variance explanations; stock adjustment control.

Month-end close and provisions
Complete assigned closing activities, accruals, provisions, expense allocations, ledger scrutiny and reconciliations within the finance calendar; retain supporting evidence.
KPIs: Close timeliness; provision accuracy; unreconciled balances.

Tax and statutory compliance
Prepare / support GST returns and reconciliations, TDS and other applicable tax / statutory submissions as assigned; track deadlines and coordinate with central finance / tax advisors. Requirements must follow current law and company delegation.
KPIs: On-time filing support; reconciliation differences; interest / penalty incidents attributable to delay.

Cash, advances and controls
Track petty cash / imprest where applicable, employee and vendor advances, ageing and settlement; ensure maker-checker controls and approvals are followed; investigate suspicious or unsupported transactions.
KPIs: Advance ageing; cash variance; control exceptions; timely settlement.

Audit and records
Maintain vouchers, invoices, tax documents, bank / payment evidence and audit trails; respond to internal / external audit queries and close findings within agreed timelines.
KPIs: Audit query closure; documentation completeness; repeat findings.

MIS and business support
Prepare daily / monthly reports on sales, collections, payables, expenses, inventory and plant cost; explain trends and support budgets and forecasts.
KPIs: MIS accuracy and timeliness; actionable variance analysis.
qualification: B.Com / M.Com / MBA Finance or equivalent
other_requirements:
Function: Finance & Accounts
Reports to: Regional / Head Office Finance or Controller; operational coordination with Plant Manager / Business Manager
Working relationships: Accounts Officers / clerical support where assigned.
Experience: Typically 4–7 years of accounting experience; plant, manufacturing, construction materials or multi-location operations experience preferred. ERP and GST working knowledge required.
Key interfaces: Plant Manager, Business Manager, Sales, Procurement, Material / Operations Officer, central Finance / Tax, banks, vendors, customers and auditors.
Work environment: Plant / area office-based; month-end and statutory deadlines may require extended hours. Tax filing ownership should follow the company’s finance structure.
Role-specific governance: Transactions must be supported by source documents, approvals and reconciliations. Statutory filing responsibilities must be allocated in line with the current finance control matrix and applicable law.

title: Logistics Incharge / Dispatch & Fleet Incharge
summary: Plan and control dispatch and fleet deployment so that concrete reaches customer sites within agreed delivery windows, with safe vehicle and pump operations, efficient utilisation, reliable tracking and controlled logistics cost.
responsibilities:
Dispatch planning
Convert confirmed orders and pour schedules into truck / pump deployment plans based on batch capacity, route, distance, site access, cycle time and fleet availability; sequence loads and manage order changes.
KPIs: On-time delivery; dispatch plan adherence; order-to-dispatch time.

Fleet utilisation and availability
Track transit mixer and pump availability, location, capacity, maintenance status and driver rosters; balance owned and hired fleet; arrange backup capacity for peak demand.
KPIs: Fleet utilisation; trips per vehicle; vehicle availability; hired-fleet cost.

Live movement and turnaround
Monitor loading, departure, travel, site arrival, waiting, discharge and return; use GPS / telematics / dispatch systems where available; intervene early on delays and long site waiting.
KPIs: Truck turnaround time; site waiting time; cycle time; delivery variance.

Customer and site coordination
Confirm site readiness, access restrictions, pump requirements, pour sequence and contact person; update customers and Sales on delays; record site-related waiting, rejected loads and cancellations with reasons.
KPIs: Delivery-related complaints; avoidable waiting; cancellation / rejection due to logistics.

Safety and statutory vehicle controls
Verify driver authorisation, fitness, permits, insurance, PUC, maintenance and other applicable vehicle documents through the responsible fleet owner / vendor; enforce speed, fatigue, PPE and site-safety rules; investigate incidents.
KPIs: Document validity; safety incidents; driver compliance; incident closure.

Cost and vendor management
Monitor fuel, tolls, hired vehicle rates, overtime, idle time, maintenance and pump deployment; validate vendor bills against trips, logs and approved rates; escalate abnormal consumption or billing.
KPIs: Logistics cost per m³ / trip; fuel variance; vendor bill accuracy; idle cost.

Maintenance and breakdown response
Coordinate preventive maintenance and breakdown support; maintain vehicle downtime records and replacement plans; avoid dispatching unsafe or unfit vehicles.
KPIs: Breakdown rate; downtime; preventive-maintenance compliance.

Records and MIS
Maintain dispatch register, trip sheets, GPS / delivery records, waiting-time logs, vehicle utilisation, vendor bills and daily / monthly performance dashboards.
KPIs: Record completeness; MIS timeliness; reconciliation accuracy.
qualification: Graduate / Diploma in Logistics, Operations, Mechanical or related discipline; equivalent logistics experience may be considered
other_requirements:
Function: Logistics / Dispatch
Reports to: Plant Manager / Business Manager or designated Logistics Head
Working relationships: Dispatchers, fleet coordinators and assigned transport / pump coordination staff; third-party fleet remains subject to contract and control arrangements.
Experience: Typically 3–6 years in fleet, dispatch, transport or RMC logistics; transit-mixer / concrete-pump coordination experience preferred.
Key interfaces: Plant Manager, batching operators, Sales, customers / site teams, drivers, pump operators, maintenance, Accounts, transport vendors and fleet owners.
Work environment: Plant / field role with shift coverage, early / late dispatches and occasional weekend or extended-hour support.
Role-specific governance: Only authorised and roadworthy vehicles / equipment should be deployed. Vehicle compliance verification and vendor responsibilities must be clearly allocated in the applicable contract and fleet-control process.
